seo.title: Remote Villages of Zanskar — 12 Days in Zanskar and Leh | Adventure Access
seo.description: Twelve days from Delhi into Zanskar: Zangla's palace, a two-day trek over a 16,500-foot pass to Dipling, and village homestays. From $4,889, double occupancy.

hero.title: Remote Villages
hero.subtitle: Village homes, a royal palace town and a two-day trek over a high pass to one of Ladakh's most traditional villages
hero.imageAlt: Green fields across a wide Zanskar valley below the mountains

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: Villages, Passes and New Friends
paragraphs: This trip pairs cultural experiences we have built over years of local relationships with hiking in some of Zanskar's most remote valleys. Anyone willing to prepare and work hard can do it, but these are still hikes for people who want to push themselves on some of the highest trails in the world.

Zanskar's culture has stayed mostly unchanged for a thousand years, so much of this journey is spent with Ladakhi people and in their homes. Time in Leh, the busy capital of Ladakh, and in Delhi rounds out the picture. Our local specialists handle everything from airport pickup to drop-off, so you can focus on the trip.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Ease In, Then Go High
dayTypes.lede: With altitudes pushing 16,000 feet, we pace the first days on purpose. What can feel like unnecessary slowness is a proven way to keep you from burning out on day two and missing the rest of the trip.

cards.title: Acclimatization days
cards.body: Days 1–3: a soft start at Nimmu House, village life with local guides, then the long drive over the passes into Zanskar.

cards.title: Hiking days
cards.body: Days 4–7: a palace hike in Zangla, then two days on foot over a pass to Dipling, with water crossings and steep climbs at altitude.

cards.title: City days
cards.body: Days 8–12: back to Leh for markets and a celebration dinner, then a final day of food and markets in Delhi before you fly home.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: Twelve Days, Village to Village
chapters.lede: Hike figures are distance, total ascent and highest point.

groups.title: Nimmu — A Soft Start at a Village Home

image.alt: A woman carrying fresh-cut greens through the fields near Nimmu

prose: Nimmu House is a traditional Ladakhi home, still lived in, that has been turned into a small hotel with excellent food. Its courtyards, luxury tents and comfortable rooms are a first way into the history and culture of the region, and a gentle place to let your body adjust.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Fly through New Delhi to Leh and drive straight to Nimmu. A tour of the house with the owner, then Asian fusion dinner.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: Breakfast at Nimmu House, then village life and local traditions with the homestay's own guides. Dinner and a campfire to close your first full day in the Himalaya.

groups.title: Zangla — Into Zanskar's Royal Capital

image.alt: Hikers on the trail toward the chortens below Zangla palace

prose: The longest drive of the trip crosses two high passes to reach Zangla, the ancient royal capital of Zanskar and one of our favorite villages. A thousand-year-old palace sits above the village, and a hidden royal stronghold waits in the hills behind it.

days.label: Day 3
days.text: About ten hours on the road, with lunch just below Sirsir La and a crossing of Singe La, the highest pass in the region, above 16,500 feet. Down to the Zanskar River and a homestay in Zangla.

days.label: Day 4
days.text: A short, hard hike to Malai Khartse, the stronghold the Zanskari kings used during raids, with water crossings and steep scrambles. Lunch at the homestay, free exploration of the main palace, then an optional village walk and an easy evening before the big hike.

groups.title: Dipling — Over the Pass to a Thousand-Year-Old Village

image.alt: A narrow trail along a rocky hillside

prose: Dipling has kept the old Ladakhi way of life for a thousand years and is one of the few villages left that still does. Reaching it takes two days on foot, with a camp at the base of the pass and the hardest climb of the trip on the second morning.

days.label: Day 5
days.text: An early start from Zangla, a drive to the trailhead, then miles of ancient yak paths to a camp at the base of one of the passes that separate Dipling from the rest of the region. Dinner cooked by your local guides. 9 mi · 2,300 ft up · high point 15,000 ft.

days.label: Day 6
days.text: Hot breakfast with chai and coffee, then a water crossing and a slow, steady climb to the top of the pass. No more climbs after this. Down into Dipling to walk the village and meet farmers and schoolchildren, then a homestay dinner. 12 mi · 2,000 ft up · high point 16,500 ft.

groups.overnight: 2 Nights · Camp below the pass, then camping in Dipling

groups.title: Lingshed and Nerak — Three Villages and High Roads

image.alt: Hikers on a ridge trail above the valley

prose: The road has nearly reached Dipling from the east, so the vehicles wait just beyond the village. From there it is a day of high roads and one more village to explore.

days.label: Day 7
days.text: A short walk out to the vehicles, then a stop in Lingshed for photos and snacks and on to Nerak, a hillside village about halfway between Zanskar and Leh. Explore its winding paths and forage for aromatic leaves. 0–5 mi, slightly downhill, depending on road construction.

groups.title: Leh — Canyon Roads and Old Markets

image.alt: Leh Palace behind the stupas of the old town

prose: Leh feels like an overgrown village with busy markets and great food. After Zanskar it can feel like a metropolis.

days.label: Day 8
days.text: Sunlit peaks and mountains shaped like weathered faces on the drive out to the main highway, lunch in Photoksar, then the smooth Leh highway. A long-overdue shower and a good meal in Leh.

days.label: Day 9
days.text: Explore the old market streets and the Central Asian Museum, or hike to Shanti Stupa or Leh Palace for views over the old town. A celebration dinner to share the week's best stories.

groups.title: Delhi — Markets, Food and Home

image.alt: An Old Delhi street at sunset

prose: A last contrast: from the rugged quiet of Ladakh to the color and noise of India's capital.

days.label: Day 10
days.text: An early flight from Leh, an afternoon and evening touring New Delhi, and dinner at an excellent local restaurant.

days.label: Day 11
days.text: A full day with our Delhi guides: food from across the subcontinent and the markets of this old Silk Road city, then dinner at our favorite Persian restaurant.

days.label: Day 12
days.text: Fly home, or ask us to extend your time with more of Delhi, the Taj Mahal or elsewhere in India.

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Fitness
cards.body: The trip is open to anyone willing to prepare, but the hikes are hard: water crossings, steep scrambles and a pass at 16,500 feet. Come ready to push yourself.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: Altitudes push 16,000 feet and above. We build up slowly over the first days, and your guides pay close attention to acclimatization the whole way.

cards.title: Local culture
cards.body: Ladakhi culture is very hospitable. Your guide will keep you informed on local customs as you go. Learn as you travel, and leave better than you came.

cards.title: Water and the land
cards.body: Instead of hundreds of plastic bottles, we provide a more sustainable way to keep you supplied with clean water, and we take our cues from local partners on how to travel well here.

cards.title: Where your money goes
cards.body: We give 3% of general revenue to sponsor children in Zanskar, so they can go to school.

cards.title: Living in India?
cards.body: Reach out to info@adventure-access.com for a modified itinerary and pricing for residents.

stays.label: Where You'll Stay
stays.heading: Village Homes, a Camp and a City Hotel
paragraphs: Nimmu House, a 5-star village home, starts the trip. Most villages in Zanskar have no hotels, so you stay in homestays, some rustic and some with more comforts, and camp on the way to Dipling. In Leh we prefer 3–4 star places with hospitable owners over glossy hotels with poor service, and in Delhi a 5-star hotel.
